previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and jaundice. Imaging revealed dilated bile ducts and lab findings consistent with biliary obstruction. He underwent an uncomplicated ERCP with sphincterotomy and successful removal of a 5mm common bile duct stone. His pain resolved post-procedure, and he tolerated advancement to a regular diet. His chronic hepatitis C and cirrhosis were stable, managed with lactulose; spironolactone and tamoxifen were held due to lack of volume overload. He remained on Bactrim for ongoing osteomyelitis prophylaxis, while ciprofloxacin and metronidazole were discontinued due to concern for bone marrow suppression. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with his PCP for blood work and surgical evaluation for cholecystectomy.
problems: Calculus of bile duct without mention of cholecystitis, with obstruction
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol

radiology_notes.text:
SHOULDER

HISTORY:  Right shoulder pain after procedure without fracture.

Four views.  Comparison with the previous study done ___.  An irregularly
shaped defect in the lateral aspect of the humeral head consistent with a
history of curettage is again demonstrated.  Visualized cortical margins
appear otherwise intact.  Bones are somewhat osteopenic as before.  There is
no evidence of dislocation.  There is no significant change.

IMPRESSION:  Post-surgical change proximal right humerus.
